notes: ACCESS: plain direct fetch (probe.py / requests) worked throughout, no blocking, exactly as the prior Home-Decor pass recorded. robots.txt checked - no anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web directive. TREE: taken from three independent sources that agreed - (1) https://www.marksandspencer.com/sitemap/uk_sitemap_home-and-furniture.xml (authoritative, and the ONLY source that exposed the level-6 nodes tv-units, dining-tables and dining-chairs); (2) the Categories facet inside each page's __NEXT_DATA__ (props.pageProps.serverSideGqlResponseFed.productPageData.search.results.facets[id=Categories]) - this facet is INCOMPLETE, it omitted dining-tables / dining-chairs / tv-units, so it was used only for corroboration; (3) each page's serverSideNavResponseFed.navigationCategoryByUrl.breadCrumbs, used to prove the real parent/child depth (confirmed TV Units is a genuine child of Bookcases & Shelves at breadcrumb position 6, and Dining Tables / Dining Chairs are children of Dining Tables & Chairs). A WebFetch render of the Furniture landing page independently confirmed the 5 top-level children and the '1 - 48 of 568 Items' header. QTY: every leaf was opened directly and read TWICE (a first read plus a fresh live re-read). For every leaf the rendered header text ('N Items', or '1 - 48 of 65 Items' on Garden Furniture) matched results.totalItems exactly, and neither value drifted between the two reads; the page h1 was also checked against the expected category name on every leaf. No qty was copied from a parent facet - the prior Home-Decor pass proved the M&S Categories facet drifts a few units from the child page's own total, so only the child page's own number was used. SANITY: numbers vary per category (no constant site-wide value) and none is suspiciously round. Guard against M&S silently serving a parent listing on a bad slug: the guessed URL .../bedroom-furniture/mattresses/natural-mattresses returned h1 'Mattresses' and total 26 (the parent's number), so it was rejected as a non-existent node; every accepted leaf had a matching h1. SCOPE: stayed inside the Home & Furniture department as instructed; food and fashion were never enumerated. Scanned the other department sitemaps (kids, gifts, style-and-living, flowers-and-plants) for furniture slugs - the only hits were /c/ editorial pages ('garden-furniture-ideas', 'sun-lounger-ideas-for-the-garden', 'outdoor-living') and /c/kids/nursery, all landing/editorial pages excluded by rule 3; no furniture listing page exists outside /l/home-and-furniture. INCLUDED beyond the Furniture department: the Nursery > Nursery Furniture branch (cots, nursery dressers/changers, nursery wardrobes, nursery furniture sets, highchairs) per the kids/nursery furniture rule. EXCLUDED: Mattresses (26) with its children Pocket Spring (21) and Anti-Allergy (9) - bedding, not furniture, and M&S splits Beds out separately so the 'Beds & Mattresses' exception did not apply; Nursery > Baby Bouncers (6) and Booster Seats (4) - titles inspected ('Alto Smart Swing Baby Bouncer', 'Tempo 3-in-1 Rocker Ivy Bouncer', 'Bug 3-in-1 Floor And Booster Seat') are infant bouncers and portable seat inserts, i.e. baby gear, so the products contradict the site's Nursery-Furniture filing; also Nursery > Travel Systems / Prams, Nursery Decor and Cot Bedding; Home Furnishings > Beanbags (11) and Pouffes (1) - the brief admits poufs only 'when the site files them as furniture/seating', and M&S files both under Home Furnishings alongside cushions, throws, rugs, curtains and bedspreads (a soft-furnishings department), not under Furniture; Bathroom (306) - its only children are Towels (236), Bath & Shower Mats (69) and Bathroom Accessories (1), so M&S sells no bathroom vanity/cabinet furniture; Garden Accessories (15), Suitcases & Luggage, Bedding, Kitchenware, Tableware, Lighting and Home Accessories (including its Storage node, standalone boxes/baskets), plus all /l/home-and-furniture/just-arrived, best-sellers, interior-trends, colour-trends, home-styles, home-promotion, our-top-picks, spring-decor, autumn-decor, cosy-home, home-essentials and university-essentials landing pages (rule 3), and the /fs5/<colour> and size filter URLs. COVERAGE CAVEAT: M&S leaves a large share of products on the parent node with no deeper subcategory (Living Room Furniture 236 vs 80 in children; Sofas 199 vs 62 in children, i.e. the actual sofas have no node of their own; Bedroom Furniture 157 vs 98). Per the mandatory deepest-URL rule those parents are emitted as grouping rows, so those residual products are not represented by any leaf qty. Each affected grouping row carries a MANUAL REVIEW flag naming the parent URL and its own verified total, in case the orchestrator prefers to record them as leaves.
